topic: Dense branching coral colonies shelter an interior stagnant zone once flow passes about 20 cm/s; branch spacing sets how far water reaches inside
summary: Densely branched coral colonies act like a solid body. Flow of about 20 cm/s wraps around the colony and leaves a stagnant pocket inside it, while sparser branching lets water reach deeper. Corals reshape with flow: compact forms under high flow, open forms with thin branches under low flow. Flow sets the diffusive boundary layer that controls passive transport of oxygen and dissolved inorganic carbon to the tissue. Geometry also shapes light: in one model, shaded rear sides get about half the incident light while light near the skeleton reaches about 1.7 times incident.

facts.claim: Densely packed branching colonies act as a solid body; flow at about 20 cm/s starts to circumvent the colony, creating a stagnant region inside.
facts.source_title: Modelling Growth and Form of the Scleractinian Coral Pocillopora verrucosa and the Influence of Hydrodynamics

facts.claim: Pocillopora verrucosa shows a compact shape under high flow and a more open growth form with thin branches under lower flow, as cited from Kaandorp (1999).
facts.source_title: Modelling Growth and Form of the Scleractinian Coral Pocillopora verrucosa and the Influence of Hydrodynamics

facts.claim: Gradients in the Diffusive Boundary Layer around corals are directly influenced by flow and drive passive diffusion of ions, dissolved inorganic carbon and oxygen at tissue level.
facts.source_title: Modelling Growth and Form of the Scleractinian Coral Pocillopora verrucosa and the Influence of Hydrodynamics

facts.claim: Colonies from low-flow sites were reported to distribute flow velocity more evenly throughout the colony interior (Chang et al., cited in the paper).
facts.source_title: Modelling Growth and Form of the Scleractinian Coral Pocillopora verrucosa and the Influence of Hydrodynamics

facts.claim: The paper states that the morphology and degree of branching in coral colonies affect both the light field and the water flow around the colony.
facts.source_title: Modeling the radiative, thermal and chemical microenvironment of 3D scanned corals

facts.claim: In a simulation of a 3D-scanned branched coral fragment, shaded rear sides received around half the incident irradiance, and light near the tissue-skeleton interface reached up to about 1.7 times incident.
facts.source_title: Modeling the radiative, thermal and chemical microenvironment of 3D scanned corals

visualisable_mechanisms.name: solid-body flow threshold
visualisable_mechanisms.description: Densely packed branches shield one another so the colony behaves as one solid body. Above about 20 cm/s, flow wraps around the outside and leaves a stagnant region inside, so the core stops being ventilated.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: A branching lattice of many nodes where inner nodes dim or fade as a flow-speed value rises past a visible 20 cm/s mark, and a stagnant core appears as a dark zone with the outer shell still lit.

visualisable_mechanisms.name: flow-set branch thinning
visualisable_mechanisms.description: Colony form tracks flow over time: strong flow favours compact, thick branches, while weak flow produces open growth with thin, widely spaced branches. Growth responds to the flow field as it changes.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: Branches accrete tip by tip over the piece; a flow value ramps up and down, and each new branch thickens or thins and its spacing tightens or opens to match, so the silhouette visibly breathes.

visualisable_mechanisms.name: boundary-layer halo
visualisable_mechanisms.description: Each branch is wrapped in a diffusive boundary layer whose thickness is set by flow. The gradients inside it drive passive diffusion of oxygen and dissolved inorganic carbon to the tissue.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: A thin translucent halo around every branch whose width shrinks with flow speed; halos from neighbouring branches merge into a single haze where spacing is tight.

visualisable_mechanisms.name: shade-and-light split
visualisable_mechanisms.description: Branch geometry splits light: rear, shaded sides receive about half the incident irradiance, while light near the skeleton can reach about 1.7 times incident in simulation.
visualisable_mechanisms.render_or_sonify_hint: Each branch is lit on one face and dim on the other; brightness peaks in the crotches between branches and falls to half on the shaded side, shifting as the colony grows.

open_questions: Does the stagnant-interior threshold near 20 cm/s hold for coral species other than Pocillopora verrucosa?
The 2023 light model did not simulate calcification; how strongly do the light and flow gradients inside a colony change calcification rate?
What flow speed in the field marks the switch between compact and open growth forms?

surprise.justification: A generalist expects each coral branch to be bathed in flow and calcify alike. In fact dense branches shield one another, and above about 20 cm/s the colony interior can become a stagnant, diffusion-limited pocket.
